newsitem.title: USA: Sears fourth-quarter profits up nearly 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Sears fourth-quarter profits up nearly 25 percent.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. posted a 24.6 percent increase in income Thursday for the fourth quarter as sales jumped 10.8 percent.
The retailer said it earned $567 million, or $1.42 a share, on sales of $12.04 billion. A year earlier, Sears earned $455 million, or $1.13 a share, on sales of $10.87 billion.
"We ended the year with excellent fourth-quarter results, which are even more impressive given the strength of last year's fourth quarter," said Chairman Arthur C. Martinez.

"December sales were strong across the board, and included our first ever back-to-back billion dollar sales weeks. Our full-line stores achieved double-digit comparable store sales increases in all apparel and softline categories as well as in computers, electronics, tools and hardware," Martinez said.
For the year, Sears earned $1.27 billion, or $3.12 a share, on sales of $38.24 billion. In 1995, the company earned $1.03 billion, or $2.53 a share, on sales of $35.0 billion.
